## React Native Project Structure Overview

Based on my thorough exploration of `/Users/stjepandzojic/projects/cloakanddagger/src`, here's the complete architectural breakdown:

### 1. TOP-LEVEL DIRECTORY STRUCTURE

```
src/
├── @types/                    # Global TypeScript type definitions
├── assets/                    # Images, icons, static resources
├── modules/                   # Feature-specific, business logic modules
├── screens/                   # Screen/page components (navigation destinations)
├── shared/                    # Reusable components, utilities, styles
└── polyfills/                 # Browser/environment compatibility polyfills
```

### 2. MODULES STRUCTURE (Feature-Scoped Organization)

Modules follow a consistent internal structure with specialization by subdirectory:

```
src/modules/
├── auth/
│   └── service/
├── call/
│   ├── components/
│   ├── jotai/                # State atoms
│   ├── provider/             # React context/providers
│   └── service/
├── encryption/
│   └── service/
├── matrix-client/
│   ├── const/                # Constants (endpoints, URLs)
│   ├── helpers/              # Utility functions
│   ├── hooks/                # React hooks
│   ├── jotai/                # State management atoms
│   ├── models/               # Data models
│   ├── providers/            # Context providers
│   ├── services/             # Business logic services
│   └── utils/                # Pure utility functions
├── navigation/
│   ├── components/
│   │   └── root-navigator/
│   └── const/
├── push-notifications/
│   ├── jotai/
│   ├── provider/
│   │   └── fragments/        # Sub-components of provider
│   ├── service/
│   └── util/
├── recorder-player/
│   ├── const/
│   ├── hooks/
│   ├── jotai/
│   ├── providers/
│   ├── services/
│   └── utils/
├── room/
│   ├── service/
│   └── utils/                # Note: has both "uitls" (typo) and "utils"
├── storage/
│   ├── hooks/
│   ├── jotai/
│   └── utils/
├── timeline/
│   ├── hooks/
│   ├── jotai/
│   ├── service/
│   ├── types/
│   └── utils/
└── verification/
    └── service/
```

**Module Organization Pattern:**
- `service/` — Business logic, API calls, external integrations
- `jotai/` — State atoms (Jotai state management)
- `provider/` — React context providers
- `utils/` — Pure utility functions
- `hooks/` — Custom React hooks
- `components/` — React components specific to this module
- `const/` — Constants (URLs, strings, values)
- `helpers/` — Helper functions (similar to utils)

### 3. SCREENS STRUCTURE (Views with Fragments Pattern)

Screen organization uses a **parent screen + fragments** pattern:

```
src/screens/
├── home/
│   ├── Home.tsx              # Main screen component
│   ├── index.ts              # Barrel export
│   └── fragments/            # Logical UI subdivisions
│       ├── filters/
│       │   ├── Filters.tsx   # Component
│       │   └── index.ts      # Export
│       ├── header/
│       │   ├── Header.tsx
│       │   └── index.ts
│       ├── new-chat-button/
│       │   ├── NewChatButton.tsx
│       │   └── index.ts
│       ├── rooms/
│       ├── rooms-list-item/
│       │   ├── RoomsListItem.tsx
│       │   ├── fragments/    # Nested fragments (2+ levels allowed)
│       │   │   ├── room-context-menu/
│       │   │   ├── room-invite-actions/
│       │   │   └── index.ts
│       │   └── index.ts
│       ├── search/
│       ├── security-filter/
│       ├── no-room-wrapper/
│       ├── protect-account-message/
│       └── index.ts          # Barrel export: re-exports all fragments
│
├── room/                      # Complex screen with 37+ fragments
│   ├── Room.tsx
│   ├── index.ts
│   └── fragments/
│       ├── message-content-bottom-sheet/
│       ├── message-content-item-list/
│       ├── deleted-message/
│       ├── file-message/
│       ├── image-message/
│       ├── date-divider/
│       ├── mention-suggestion-list/
│       ├── call-button/
│       ├── grouped-info-messages/
│       ├── identity-violation-banner/
│       ├── input-message-payload/
│       └── ... (30+ more)
│
├── settings/
│   ├── Settings.tsx
│   ├── index.ts
│   └── fragments/
│       ├── settings-list-item/
│       ├── sign-out-bottom-sheet/
│       ├── user-info-item/
│       └── index.ts
│
├── splash/                    # Simple screen, no fragments
│   ├── Splash.tsx
│   └── index.ts
│
├── about/                     # Simple screen, no fragments
│   └── ...
│
└── index.ts                   # Root barrel export (48 screens)
```

**Key Patterns:**
- Each screen has its own directory
- Main component named `ScreenName.tsx` (PascalCase)
- `index.ts` file exports the main component using barrel export
- **Complex screens** break UI into `fragments/` subfolder
- Each fragment has its own directory with component file + `index.ts`
- Fragments can have **nested fragments** (e.g., `rooms-list-item/fragments/room-context-menu/`)
- Fragment folder structure mirrors main screen structure

### 4. SHARED FOLDER STRUCTURE (Reusable Assets)

```
src/shared/
├── components/               # Reusable UI components
│   ├── button/              # Complex component with sub-variants
│   │   ├── index.tsx        # Namespace export (exports Button object)
│   │   ├── button.types.ts  # Type definitions
│   │   ├── const/
│   │   │   └── button-size.ts
│   │   └── fragments/       # Button variants
│   │       ├── Primary.tsx
│   │       ├── Secondary.tsx
│   │       ├── Ghost.tsx
│   │       ├── Outline.tsx
│   │       ├── OutlinePrimary.tsx
│   │       ├── Warning.tsx
│   │       ├── Wrapper.tsx
│   │       ├── ButtonContent.tsx
│   │       └── index.ts
│   ├── loading/
│   │   ├── Loading.tsx
│   │   └── index.ts
│   ├── screen-layout/
│   │   ├── ScreenLayout.tsx
│   │   └── index.ts
│   ├── user-profile-image/
│   │   ├── UserProfileImage.tsx
│   │   └── index.ts
│   ├── radio-button/
│   ├── input/
│   ├── user-image/
│   ├── room-image/
│   ├── member-details-bottom-sheet/
│   ├── pin-indicator/
│   ├── delivery-status/
│   ├── image-viewer-modal/
│   ├── go-back-header/
│   ├── seen-by/
│   ├── check-button/
│   ├── video-viewer-modal/
│   ├── message-timestamp/
│   └── index.ts            # Barrel export
│
├── hooks/                   # Reusable React hooks
│
├── utils/                   # Shared utility functions
│   ├── atom-state-factory.ts
│   ├── get-level-label.ts
│   ├── image-caching.ts
│   └── index.ts            # Barrel export
│
├── const/                   # Shared constants
│   ├── theme-default.ts
│   ├── skeleton-default.ts
│   ├── toast-config.tsx
│   ├── mocked-auth-data.ts
│   └── index.ts
│
├── styles/                  # Shared styling (theme, colors, text sizes)
│   ├── colors.styles.ts
│   ├── text.styles.ts
│   └── index.ts
│
└── index.ts               # Root barrel export
```

### 5. NAMING CONVENTIONS & PATTERNS

#### File Naming:
- **Component files:** PascalCase (`Home.tsx`, `Filters.tsx`, `Primary.tsx`)
- **Utility/service files:** camelCase or kebab-case (`get-level-label.ts`, `getEventId.ts`)
- **Type files:** kebab-case with `.types` suffix (`button.types.ts`)
- **Const files:** kebab-case with `.ts` suffix (`button-size.ts`)
- **Index files:** Always `index.ts` for barrel exports

#### Barrel Export Pattern:
Every folder has an `index.ts` that re-exports its contents:

```typescript
// src/screens/home/fragments/filters/index.ts
export * from "./Filters";

// src/shared/components/button/index.tsx
import { Primary, Secondary, Ghost, ... } from "./fragments";
export const Button = { Primary, Secondary, Ghost, ... };
```

#### Fragment Naming:
- Fragments are always PascalCase folders with a component file inside
- `fragments/` directory signals "sub-components of this parent"
- Can nest multiple levels deep: `screen → fragments → fragment → fragments → sub-fragment`

### 6. UTILITY FUNCTION ORGANIZATION

**Pattern 1: Dedicated Utility Files** (most common)
Each utility lives in its own file with a focused, exported function:

```typescript
// src/modules/matrix-client/utils/getEventId.ts
export const getEventId = (item: EventTimelineItem) => { ... };
export const getItemUniqueKey = (item: EventTimelineItem) => { ... };
export const getTransactionId = (item: EventTimelineItem) => { ... };
```

Each utility file is then re-exported via an `index.ts`:
```typescript
// src/modules/matrix-client/utils/index.ts
export * from "./getEventId";
export * from "./getMessageType";
export * from "./getHttpUriForMxc";
// ... etc
```

**Pattern 2: Component-Scoped Constants** (in const subfolder)
Style configs, sizes, and constants live in `const/`:
```typescript
// src/shared/components/button/const/button-size.ts
export const ButtonSize = {
  normal: { paddings: [12, 24] },
  small: { paddings: [8, 16] },
};
```

**Pattern 3: Utilities Inside Component Folders** (rarely)
Simple, reusable utilities are in dedicated module `utils/` folders:
```typescript
// src/modules/recorder-player/utils/
├── get-time-duration.ts
├── remove-file.ts
├── round-milli-to-seconds.ts
└── index.ts
```

### 7. REPRESENTATIVE EXAMPLES

#### Example 1: Simple Screen (No Fragments)
```
src/screens/splash/
├── Splash.tsx         # 60+ lines, contains all logic and UI
└── index.ts           # export * from "./Splash"
```

#### Example 2: Complex Screen (With Fragments)
```
src/screens/home/
├── Home.tsx           # Orchestrates fragments, ~36 lines
├── index.ts
└── fragments/
    ├── header/
    │   ├── Header.tsx
    │   └── index.ts
    ├── filters/
    │   ├── Filters.tsx
    │   └── index.ts
    ├── rooms/
    ├── rooms-list-item/
    │   ├── RoomsListItem.tsx   # 6786 bytes
    │   ├── fragments/          # Nested fragments!
    │   │   ├── room-context-menu/
    │   │   ├── room-invite-actions/
    │   │   └── index.ts
    │   └── index.ts
    └── index.ts       # Barrel exports all fragments for parent
```

#### Example 3: Feature Module with Utilities
```
src/modules/matrix-client/
├── services/
│   └── MatrixCore.ts
├── utils/
│   ├── getEventId.ts        # Multiple exports per file
│   ├── getMessageType.ts
│   ├── fetchMedia.ts
│   └── index.ts             # Barrel export
├── const/
│   ├── matrix-endpoints.ts
│   └── sygnal-url.ts
├── helpers/
├── hooks/
├── jotai/
└── providers/
```

#### Example 4: Complex Shared Component (Button)
```
src/shared/components/button/
├── index.tsx               # Namespace object export
├── button.types.ts         # Shared prop types
├── const/
│   └── button-size.ts
└── fragments/              # Button variants
    ├── Primary.tsx
    ├── Secondary.tsx
    ├── Outline.tsx
    ├── Ghost.tsx
    ├── Warning.tsx
    ├── Wrapper.tsx
    ├── ButtonContent.tsx    # Shared by multiple variants
    └── index.ts
```

### 8. KEY OBSERVATIONS

1. **Consistency:** Every folder with exported content has an `index.ts` barrel export
2. **Scalability:** Fragments can nest indefinitely (home → rooms-list-item → room-context-menu)
3. **Separation of concerns:** Service/hooks/utils live in separate folders within modules
4. **Module isolation:** Each module (auth, call, encryption, etc.) is self-contained
5. **Flat utility files:** Most utilities are single-file exports with related functions grouped
6. **Component composition:** Complex components use fragments for readability; simple screens remain flat
7. **Reusable assets:** shared/ contains only truly shared components, hooks, and utilities
8. **State management:** Jotai atoms live in dedicated `jotai/` folders within modules

This architecture balances developer experience (easy to find and navigate) with scalability (fragments prevent monolithic screens).
